Terminology & Definitions

TermDefinition
AssetA discovered system, endpoint, service or domain under assessment (e.g. a scanned host). This assessment: 3 discovered asset(s) (1 in the formal asset inventory; the remainder are scanned endpoints attributed from findings evidence).
Cryptographic Component (CBOM)An individual algorithm, cipher suite, key, certificate or protocol usage discovered inside assets — one asset typically contains many components. This assessment: 39 component(s).
PQC-Ready ComponentA CBOM component already using NIST PQC (FIPS 203/204/205) or hybrid cryptography. This assessment: 1 of 39 (2.6%). The "PQC-Ready Components" readiness factor is this percentage — a component share, never an asset count.
PQC-Ready AssetAn asset whose observed cryptography is entirely PQC or hybrid. This assessment: 0 of 1 inventoried asset(s). Distinct from PQC-ready components by definition.
Finding vs Consolidated FindingA finding is one detected cryptographic weakness instance; consolidated findings group instances by root cause so an issue is counted once for decision-making.
Quantum Readiness vs Quantum RiskReadiness (higher is better) measures migration progress and governance; risk (lower is better) measures exposure to future quantum decryption. They are computed independently and reconciled in their methodology sections.
Runtime VisibilityMeasured exclusively from live runtime cryptographic telemetry. When no runtime telemetry exists the factor is reported as "Not Measured" and excluded from the readiness formula — it is never approximated from scan activity.
